items.item: The struct's data loss in this topic is two different failure modes, not one: the scroll event loses depth_pct because no column exists for it at all, while button_id: "unknown" is dropped because a column exists but can't hold the value's actual type — both are silent, but for different reasons.

items.item: The Variant metadata dictionary is shared across every value column of the same Variant, including shredded typed_value columns — field names are stored once, not once per record, which is why the metadata stays tiny even as the number of records grows.

items.item: Shredding is decided per field, not per record or per table — this topic's own button_id column shows both a fully-shredded case (an int) and a fallback case (a string) existing for the same field across different records.

A field being 'always shredded' in this topic's 6-record sample (event_type) is a property of this sample, not a guarantee of the Variant type itself — a later record with a non-string event_type would fall back exactly as button_id does for record 6.

The size comparison in this topic understates shredding's real-world benefit on purpose: a 6-record sample is too small to show the compounding effect of typed-column compression and run-length encoding that a real columnar file gets on millions of rows.

The query-cost claim (0 residual bytes read for a shredded event_type filter) is a stronger and more general result than the size claim, because it holds even when shredding barely shrinks the file at all.

at.step: Reveal: shredding's real win isn't size

items.item: Partial shredding (VariantShredding.md's own term) is what happens to records 2 and 3 in this topic: a real field survives in the residual value column precisely because it wasn't one of the fields chosen to shred, not because shredding itself failed.

This topic's encoder implements only the primitive types its own dataset needs (null, int32, short string, object); the specification defines many more (decimals, dates, timestamps, arrays, UUIDs) on the identical header-byte pattern, disclosed rather than silently left out.

Readers must still be able to read an unshredded value+metadata group even on a table where some files shred a field and others don't — this topic's own 'Variant (unshredded)' step is exactly that minimum guaranteed form.

items.item: The struct's silent data loss in this topic is the same failure class topic 7's truncated-statistics bug warned about: a reader (or in this case a schema) trusting a shape that isn't actually true of the data produces wrong results with no visible error.
